summary: A 16-bit I2C temperature sensor. One register holds the result, one holds configuration and flags, two hold alert limits, and one identifies the chip.

cite.q: 02h R/W 6000h(1) THigh_Limit Temperature high limit register

facts.text: One count of the result register is 7.8125 milli-degrees C; the value is two's complement.
Until the first conversion finishes after a reset, the result register reads -256 C (0x8000).

cite.q: the temperature register reads –256 °C until the first conversion

facts.text: Data_Ready (Configuration bit 13) is cleared by reading either the Configuration or the result register.

cite.q: read the configuration register or the temperature result register to clear the Data_Ready flag

facts.text: HIGH_Alert (bit 15) is set when a result is above the high limit.

cite.q: Set when the conversion result is higher than the high limit

facts.text: LOW_Alert (bit 14) is set when a result is below the low limit.

cite.q: Set when the conversion result is lower than the low limit

facts.text: The high and low alert flags clear when the Configuration register is read.

cite.q: Cleared on read of configuration register

facts.text: The reset configuration (CONV=100) gives a one-second conversion cycle at any averaging setting.
Writing 1 to Soft_Reset (bit 1) resets the device; the bit always reads back 0.

cite.q: triggers software reset with a duration of 2 ms

facts.text: One conversion takes about 15.5 ms typical; averaging repeats it, so the first result arrives after avg x 15.5 ms (derived, not stated).

notModeled: One-shot and shutdown modes (the MOD bits are stored but ignored)
EEPROM registers, temperature offset and the ALERT pin
Thermal (therm) alert mode: only alert mode is modeled
Noise, accuracy and self-heating: the sensor returns exactly the temperature you set, rounded to one count
